correctness.rationale: Complete poset generation by adjoining new maximal elements over all lower ideals is mathematically exhaustive. Strict-relation isomorphism backtracking is exact; 1, 2, 5, 16, 63, 318, 2045, 16999 totals match independently published Brinkmann–McKay tables. Joint refinement by all three strict-order atomic relations is exactly C2 equivalence by the standard finite binary-relational colour-refinement theorem. Running verify.py reads the bundled witnesses.json, confirms all class totals and that precisely two eight-point classes have two nonisomorphic members, and checks no earlier collisions. Finite exhaustion proves only n≤8, not a general arbitrary-n statement.

value.rationale: The result gives the sharp first failure of a fundamental logic invariant for an intrinsically natural structure class, partial orders. It classifies the entire first boundary layer (exactly two doubletons among 16999 poset types), discriminating two structurally distinct mechanisms: disconnected-vs-connected regular incidence in height two and misaligned vs crossed middle incidence in height three. The precise cutoff and witnesses are reproducible and provide a concrete benchmark for two-variable logic on finite orders; no downstream theorem or arbitrary parameter-selection claim is needed.
